title: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce - Business Studies - Distribution
exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The commercial process of ensuring that finished goods are moved from the point of manufacture to the point where they are needed by the final user is called
questions.explain: **Distribution** is the act of dispersing or moving goods and services from the manufacturer/producer through various intermediaries to the final consumer.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The specific path or route through which goods flow from the producer to the final consumer is formally referred to as the
questions.explain: The **chain of distribution** (or channel of distribution) describes the path that goods take as title and physical possession move from the producer to the ultimate consumer.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following represents the normal and most complete channel of distribution for consumer goods?
questions.explain: The traditional channel of distribution starts with the **Producer**, goes to the **Wholesaler** (who buys in bulk), then to the **Retailer** (who breaks bulk), and finally to the **Consumer**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the chain of distribution, the primary function of the producer is to
options: break bulk into single units for consumers
provide small daily loans to local hawkers
create and package the goods to satisfy wants
consume the goods to end the production cycle
questions.explain: The **producer** or manufacturer initiates the channel by actually creating, processing, and packaging the goods intended for market consumption.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The specific commercial function of buying goods in massive quantities from the manufacturer and dividing them into smaller manageable quantities for the retailer is known as
questions.explain: **Breaking bulk** is the core function of the wholesaler. They buy huge volumes (bulk) from producers and divide them into smaller batches that retailers can afford.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: How does the wholesaler typically provide financial assistance to the manufacturer in the channel of distribution?
options: By granting bank overdrafts to the manufacturer
By prompt or advance payment for bulk orders
By selling goods on credit directly to the final consumer
By physically printing the national currency
questions.explain: Wholesalers help finance the manufacturer's operations **by paying promptly or even paying in advance** for massive bulk orders, giving the manufacturer immediate cash to continue production.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which member of the distribution channel traditionally performs the function of stocking a wide variety of goods and providing direct credit facilities to the final consumer?
questions.explain: The **retailer** operates close to the consumers, stocks a wide variety of products from different wholesalers, and often allows trusted consumers to buy on credit.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Who is the last link in the chain of distribution, responsible for using up the goods or services?
questions.explain: The **consumer** is the ultimate end-user in the distribution channel. Their act of consumption completes the entire commercial process.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: According to the principles of commerce, the process of production is completely achieved and ends ONLY when the
options: goods are securely packed in the warehouse
wholesaler purchases the goods from the factory
goods successfully reach the final consumer
manufacturer prints the price tag on the item
questions.explain: Production is defined as the creation of goods and services to satisfy human wants. Therefore, production is not complete until the goods **reach the final consumer** who uses them.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Individuals or corporate bodies legally authorized by government regulatory agencies to sell and distribute specific industrial and domestic chemicals are known as
questions.explain: Chemicals are sensitive and potentially dangerous. The law requires that they are distributed strictly by **licensed chemical vendors** who are trained and monitored by regulators.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A standard ethical procedure in the handling and distribution of hazardous chemicals is to ensure that they are
options: transported in properly labeled and tightly sealed containers
packed together in the same truck with fresh food items
sold in open markets without any hazard warning labels
exposed to direct sunlight to maintain a warm temperature
questions.explain: To prevent leaks, toxic exposure, or fire, chemicals must be **transported in properly labeled and tightly sealed containers**, ensuring handlers know the exact contents and risks.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: What is a major environmental effect of the wrong handling and improper distribution of industrial chemicals?
options: Rapid increase in agricultural crop yield
Severe pollution of water bodies and soil
Expansion of local retail market stalls
Reduction in the cost of imported goods
questions.explain: Improper handling, spills, or illegal dumping of chemicals during distribution directly causes **severe pollution of water bodies and soil**, leading to environmental degradation.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct health consequence of workers handling toxic chemicals without proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?
options: An increase in their monthly basic salary
Severe skin burns and respiratory diseases
Immediate promotion to a management position
questions.explain: Failing to use proper handling techniques and PPE when distributing chemicals exposes workers directly to fumes and corrosive liquids, leading to **skin burns and respiratory diseases**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a manufacturer decides to open its own branded showroom and sell its manufactured goods directly to the final consumers, which traditional middlemen are eliminated from the channel?
questions.explain: By selling directly (Manufacturer $\rightarrow$ Consumer), the producer effectively bypasses or eliminates the traditional distribution middlemen, namely **the wholesaler and the retailer**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In the distribution network, the final consumer provides vital feedback through the retailer. This feedback is primarily important because it helps the producer to
options: know exactly how to increase government excise taxes
improve the quality of future goods to better satisfy wants
print out fake receipts for wholesale purchases
smuggle defective goods across international borders
questions.explain: Feedback flows backward up the distribution channel. Consumers complain or praise goods to retailers, who inform wholesalers/producers, enabling the producer to **improve product quality**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Regulatory bodies in Nigeria, such as NAFDAC or SON, heavily monitor the distribution channels of chemicals in order to
options: ensure that all chemicals are completely removed from factories
stop manufacturing companies from making any form of profit
prevent the illegal circulation of harmful, fake, or expired substances
force licensed vendors to distribute all their chemicals for free
questions.explain: The primary role of these regulators is public safety; they monitor distribution to **prevent the illegal circulation of harmful, fake, or expired substances** into the consumer market.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
